Configuration table for each System Monitor/ADC device in the system.
Initializes a specific XSysMon device instance.

detaileddescription.para: Call this function prior to using the System Monitor/ADC device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XSysMon device configuration structure.

Device base address in the virtual memory address space. If the address translation is not used then the physical address is passed. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping is changed after this function is invoked.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if successful.

simplesect.para: The user needs to first call the XSysMon_LookupConfig() API which returns the Configuration structure pointer which is passed as a parameter to the XSysMon_CfgInitialize() API.

briefdescription.para: Forces a software reset of the complete SystemMonitor/ADC Hard Macro and the SYSMON ADC Core Logic.

simplesect.para: The Control registers in the SystemMonitor/ADC Hard Macro are not affected by this reset, only the Status registers are reset. Refer to the device data sheet for the device status and register values after the reset. Use the XSysMon_ResetAdc() to reset only the SystemMonitor/ADC Hard Macro.

briefdescription.para: Reads the contents of the Status Register.

simplesect.para: A 32-bit value representing the contents of the Status Register. Use the XSM_SR_*_MASK constants defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the returned value.

briefdescription.para: Reads the contents of the Alarm Output Register.

simplesect.para: A 32-bit value read from the Alarm Output Register. Use the XSM_AOR_*_MASK constants defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the value.

briefdescription.para: Starts an ADC conversion in Single Channel event driven sampling mode.

detaileddescription.para: The EOC bit in the Status Register is set once the conversion finishes. Refer to the device specification for more details.

simplesect.para: The default state of the CONVST bit is a logic 0. The conversion is started when the CONVST bit is set to 1 from 0. This bit is cleared in this function so that the next conversion can be started by setting this bit.

briefdescription.para: Resets the SystemMonitor/ADC Hard Macro in the device.

simplesect.para: The Control registers in the SystemMonitor/ADC Hard Macro are not affected by this reset, only the Status registers are reset. This reset causes the ADC to begin with a new conversion. Refer to the device data sheet for the device status and register values after the reset. Use the XSysMon_Reset() API to reset both the SystemMonitor/ADC Hard Macro and the SYSMON ADC Core Logic.

briefdescription.para: Gets the ADC converted data for the specified channel.

parameterdescription.para: Channel number. Use the XSM_CH_* defined in the file xsysmon.h. The valid channels are 0 to 5 and 16 to 31 for all the device families. Channel 6 is valid for 7 Series and Zynq. Channel 13, 14, 15 are valid for Zynq. 32 to 35 are valid for Ultrascale.

simplesect.para: A 16-bit value representing the ADC converted data for the specified channel. The System Monitor/ADC device guarantees a 10 bit resolution for the ADC converted data and data is the 10 MSB bits of the 16 data read from the device.
The channels 7,8,9 are used for calibration of the device and hence there is no associated data with this channel. Make sure that the proper channel number is passed.

briefdescription.para: Gets the calibration coefficient data for the specified parameter.

parameterdescription.para: Calibration coefficient to be read. Use XSM_CALIB_* constants defined in xsysmon.h to specify the calibration coefficient to be read.

simplesect.para: A 16-bit value representing the calibration coefficient. The System Monitor/ADC device guarantees a 10 bit resolution for the ADC converted data and data is the 10 MSB bits of the 16 data read from the device.

briefdescription.para: Reads the Minimum/Maximum measurement for one of the listed parameters.

detaileddescription.para:
The parameter is one of the following:
Minimum Temperature (XSM_MIN_TEMP) - All families
Minimum VCCINT (XSM_MIN_VCCINT) - All families
Minimum VCCAUX (XSM_MIN_VCCAUX) - All families
Maximum Temperature (XSM_MAX_TEMP) - All families
Maximum VCCINT (XSM_MAX_VCCINT) - All families
Maximum VCCAUX (XSM_MAX_VCCAUX) - All families
Maximum VCCBRAM (XSM_MAX_VCCBRAM) - 7 series and Zynq only
Minimum VCCBRAM (XSM_MIN_VCCBRAM) - 7 series and Zynq only
Maximum VCCPINT (XSM_MAX_VCCPINT) - Zynq only
Maximum VCCPAUX (XSM_MAX_VCCPAUX) - Zynq only
Maximum VCCPDRO (XSM_MAX_VCCPDRO) - Zynq only
Minimum VCCPINT (XSM_MIN_VCCPINT) - Zynq only
Minimum VCCPAUX (XSM_MIN_VCCPAUX) - Zynq only
Minimum VCCPDRO (XSM_MIN_VCCPDRO) - Zynq only
Maximum VUSER0 (XSM_MAX_VUSR0) - Ultrascale
Maximum VUSER1 (XSM_MAX_VUSR1) - Ultrascale
Maximum VUSER2 (XSM_MAX_VUSR2) - Ultrascale
Maximum VUSER3 (XSM_MAX_VUSR3) - Ultrascale
Minimum VUSER0 (XSM_MIN_VUSR0) - Ultrascale
Minimum VUSER1 (XSM_MIN_VUSR1) - Ultrascale
Minimum VUSER2 (XSM_MIN_VUSR2) - Ultrascale
Minimum VUSER3 (XSM_MIN_VUSR3) - Ultrascale

parameterdescription.para: Parameter for which the Minimum/Maximum measurement has to be read. Use XSM_MAX_* and XSM_MIN_* constants defined in xsysmon.h to specify the data to be read.

simplesect.para: A 16-bit value representing the maximum/minimum measurement for specified parameter. The System Monitor/ADC device guarantees a 10 bit resolution for the ADC converted data and data is the 10 MSB bits of 16 bit data read from the device.

briefdescription.para: Sets the number of averaging samples for all channels.

detaileddescription.para: The averaging applies to both single channel mode and sequence mode of operation.

parameterdescription.para:
Number of samples of averaging programmed to the Configuration Register 0. Use the XSM_AVG_* definitions defined in xsysmon.h file :
XSM_AVG_0_SAMPLES for no averaging
XSM_AVG_16_SAMPLES for 16 samples of averaging
XSM_AVG_64_SAMPLES for 64 samples of averaging
XSM_AVG_256_SAMPLES for 256 samples of averaging.

briefdescription.para: Returns the number of averaging samples configured for all channels in the Configuration Register 0.

simplesect.para:
The averaging read from the Configuration Register 0 is returned. Use the XSM_AVG_* bit definitions defined in xsysmon.h file to interpret the returned value :
XSM_AVG_0_SAMPLES means no averaging.
XSM_AVG_16_SAMPLES means 16 samples of averaging.
XSM_AVG_64_SAMPLES means 64 samples of averaging.
XSM_AVG_256_SAMPLES means 256 samples of averaging.

memberdef.argsstring: (XSysMon *InstancePtr, u8 Channel, int IncreaseAcqCycles, int IsEventMode, int IsDifferentialMode)
memberdef.name: XSysMon_SetSingleChParams

briefdescription.para: Sets the given parameters in the Configuration Register 0 in single channel mode.

parameterdescription.para: Channel number for conversion. The valid channels are 0 to 5, 8, and 16 to 31. Channel 6 is valid for 7 series and Zynq XADC. Channel 32 to 35 are valid for Ultrascale.

Boolean parameter which specifies whether the Acquisition time for the external channels has to be increased to 10 ADCCLK cycles (specify TRUE) or remain at the default 4 ADCCLK cycles (specify FALSE). This parameter is only valid for the external channels.
Boolean parameter that specifies continuous sampling (specify FALSE) or event driven sampling mode (specify TRUE) for the given channel.
Boolean parameter which specifies unipolar(specify FALSE) or differential mode (specify TRUE) for the analog inputs. The input mode is only valid for the external channels.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the given values were written successfully to the Configuration Register 0.
XST_FAILURE if the channel sequencer is enabled or the input parameters are not valid for the selected channel.
The number of samples for the averaging for all the channels is set by using the function XSysMon_SetAvg.

The calibration of the device is done by doing a ADC conversion on the calibration channel(channel 8). The input parameters IncreaseAcqCycles, IsDifferentialMode and IsEventMode are not valid for this channel.

briefdescription.para: Enables the alarm outputs for the specified alarms.

detaileddescription.para: The alarms are set in the Configuration Registers 1 and 3: - OT for Over Temperature (XSM_CFR_OT_MASK) - ALM0 for On board Temperature (XSM_CFR_ALM_TEMP_MASK) - ALM1 for VCCINT (XSM_CFR_ALM_VCCINT_MASK) - ALM2 for VCCAUX (XSM_CFR_ALM_VCCAUX_MASK) - ALM3 for VBRAM (XSM_CFR_ALM_VBRAM_MASK)for 7 Series and Zynq - ALM4 for VCCPINT (XSM_CFR_ALM_VCCPINT_MASK) for Zynq - ALM5 for VCCPAUX (XSM_CFR_ALM_VCCPAUX_MASK) for Zynq - ALM6 for VCCPDRO (XSM_CFR_ALM_VCCPDRO_MASK) for Zynq - ALM8 for VUSER0 (XSM_CFR_ALM_VUSR0_MASK) for Ultrascale - ALM9 for VUSER1 (XSM_CFR_ALM_VUSR1_MASK) for Ultrascale - ALM10 for VUSER2 (XSM_CFR_ALM_VUSR2_MASK) for Ultrascale - ALM11 for VUSER3 (XSM_CFR_ALM_VUSR3_MASK) for Ultrascale

parameterdescription.para: Bit-mask of the alarm outputs to be enabled in the Configuration Register 1. Bit positions of 1 enable and bit positions of 0 disable the outputs. This mask is formed by OR'ing XSM_CFR_ALM_*_MASK, XSM_CFR_ALM_*_MASK and XSM_CFR_OT_MASK masks defined in xsysmon_hw.h.

simplesect.para: The implementation of the alarm enables in the Configuration register 1 is such that the alarms for bit positions of 1 are disabled and alarms for bit positions of 0 are enabled. The alarm outputs specified by the AlmEnableMask are negated before writing to the Configuration Register 1.

briefdescription.para: Gets the status of the alarm output enables in the Configuration Register 1.

detaileddescription.para:
InstancePtr
Pointer to the XSysMon instance.
This is the bit-mask of the enabled alarm outputs in the Configuration Register 1. Use the masks XSM_CFR_ALM_*, XSM_CFR_ALM*_* and XSM_CFR_OT_MASK defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the returned value. Bit positions of 1 indicate that the alarm output is enabled. Bit positions of 0 indicate that the alarm output is disabled.

simplesect.para: The implementation of the alarm enables in the Configuration register 1 is such that alarms for the bit positions of 1 are disabled and alarms for bit positions of 0 are enabled. The enabled alarm outputs returned by this function is the negated value of the the data read from the Configuration Register 1.

briefdescription.para: Enables the specified calibration in the Configuration Register 1.

detaileddescription.para: The calibration is one of the following: - XSM_CFR1_CAL_ADC_OFFSET_MASK : Calibration 0 -ADC offset correction - XSM_CFR1_CAL_ADC_GAIN_OFFSET_MASK : Calibration 1 -ADC gain and offset correction - XSM_CFR1_CAL_PS_OFFSET_MASK : Calibration 2 -Power Supply sensor offset correction - XSM_CFR1_CAL_PS_GAIN_OFFSET_MASK : Calibration 3 -Power Supply sensor gain and offset correction - XSM_CFR1_CAL_DISABLE_MASK : No Calibration

parameterdescription.para: Calibration to be applied. Use XSM_CFR1_CAL*_* bits defined in xsysmon_hw.h. Multiple calibrations can be enabled at a time by oring the XSM_CFR1_CAL_ADC_* and XSM_CFR1_CAL_PS_* bits. Calibration can be disabled by specifying XSM_CFR1_CAL_DISABLE_MASK.

briefdescription.para: Reads the value of the calibration enables from the Configuration Register 1.

simplesect.para:
The value of the calibration enables in the Configuration Register 1 :
XSM_CFR1_CAL_ADC_OFFSET_MASK : ADC offset correction.
XSM_CFR1_CAL_ADC_GAIN_OFFSET_MASK : ADC gain and offset correction.
XSM_CFR1_CAL_PS_OFFSET_MASK : Power Supply sensor offset correction.
XSM_CFR1_CAL_PS_GAIN_OFFSET_MASK : Power Supply sensor gain and offset correction.
XSM_CFR1_CAL_DISABLE_MASK : No Calibration.

briefdescription.para: Sets the specified Channel Sequencer Mode in Configuration Register 1.

detaileddescription.para:
The mode is one of the following:
Default safe mode (XSM_SEQ_MODE_SAFE)
One pass through sequence (XSM_SEQ_MODE_ONEPASS)
Continuous channel sequencing (XSM_SEQ_MODE_CONTINPASS)
Single Channel/Sequencer off (XSM_SEQ_MODE_SINGCHAN)
Simultaneous sampling mode (XSM_SEQ_MODE_SIMUL)
Independent mode (XSM_SEQ_MODE_INDEPENDENT)

parameterdescription.para: Sequencer mode to be set. Use XSM_SEQ_MODE_* bits defined in xsysmon.h.

simplesect.para: Only one of the modes can be enabled at a time.

briefdescription.para: Gets the channel sequencer mode from the Configuration Register 1.

simplesect.para:
The channel sequencer mode :
XSM_SEQ_MODE_SAFE : Default safe mode.
XSM_SEQ_MODE_ONEPASS : One pass through sequence.
XSM_SEQ_MODE_CONTINPASS : Continuous channel sequencing.
XSM_SEQ_MODE_SINGCHAN : Single channel/Sequencer off.
XSM_SEQ_MODE_SIMUL : Simultaneous sampling mode.
XSM_SEQ_MODE_INDEPENDENT : Independent mode.

briefdescription.para: Enables the Event mode or Continuous mode in the sequencer mode.

parameterdescription.para: Boolean parameter that specifies continuous sampling (specify FALSE) or event driven sampling mode (specify TRUE) for the given channel.

simplesect.para: The Event mode is only available in 7 Series XADC and Zynq. This API should be used only with 7 Series XADC and Zynq .

briefdescription.para: Enables the external mux and connects a channel to the mux.

parameterdescription.para: Channel number used to connect to the external Mux. The valid channels are 0 to 6, 8, and 16 to 31.

simplesect.para: The External Mux is only available in 7 Series and Zynq XADC. This API should be used only with 7 Series and Zynq XADC.

briefdescription.para: Sets the ADCCLK frequency by configuring the DCLK to ADCCLK ratio in the Configuration Register #2.

parameterdescription.para:
Clock divisor used to derive ADCCLK from DCLK. Valid values of the divisor are
8 to 255 for V5 SysMon.
0 to 255 for V6/7 Series and Zynq XADC. Values 0, 1, 2 are all mapped to 2. Refer to the device specification for more details.

simplesect.para:
- The ADCCLK is an internal clock used by the ADC and is synchronized to the DCLK clock. The ADCCLK is equal to DCLK divided by the user selection in the Configuration Register 2.
There is no Assert on the minimum value of the Divisor. Users must take care such that the minimum value of Divisor used is 8, in case of V5 SysMon.

briefdescription.para: Gets the ADCCLK divisor from the Configuration Register 2.

simplesect.para: The divisor read from the Configuration Register 2.
The ADCCLK is an internal clock used by the ADC and is synchronized to the DCLK clock. The ADCCLK is equal to DCLK divided by the user selection in the Configuration Register 2.

briefdescription.para: Enables the specified channels in the ADC Channel Selection Sequencer Registers.

detaileddescription.para: The sequencer must be in the Safe Mode before writing to these registers.

parameterdescription.para: Bit mask of all the channels to be enabled. Use XSM_SEQ_CH_* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to specify the Channel numbers. A bit set to 1 enables and a bit set to 0 disables the channel. The ChEnableMask is a 64 bit mask that is written to the three 16 bit ADC Channel Selection Sequencer Registers.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the given values were written successfully to the ADC Channel Selection Sequencer Registers.
XST_FAILURE if the channel sequencer is enabled.

briefdescription.para: Gets the channel enable bits status from the ADC Channel Selection Sequencer Registers.

simplesect.para: Gets the channel enable bits. Use XSM_SEQ_CH_* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the Channel numbers. Bit masks of 1 are the channels that are enabled and bit mask of 0 are the channels that are disabled.

briefdescription.para: Enables averaging for the specified channels in the ADC Channel Averaging Enable Sequencer Registers.

detaileddescription.para: The sequencer must be in the Safe Mode before writing to these registers.

parameterdescription.para: Bit mask of all the channels for which averaging is to be enabled. Use XSM_SEQ_CH__* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to specify the Channel numbers. Averaging is enabled for bit masks of 1 and disabled for bit mask of 0. The AvgEnableChMask is a 64 bit mask that is written to the three 16 bit ADC Channel Averaging Enable Sequencer Registers.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the given values were written successfully to the ADC Channel Averaging Enables Sequencer Registers.
XST_FAILURE if the channel sequencer is enabled.

briefdescription.para: Returns the channels for which averaging is enabled in the ADC Channel Averaging Enables Sequencer Registers.

simplesect.para: The status of averaging (enabled/disabled) for all the channels. Use XSM_SEQ_CH__* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the Channel numbers. Bit masks of 1 are the channels for which averaging is enabled and bit mask of 0 are the channels for averaging is disabled.

briefdescription.para: Sets the analog input mode for the specified channels in the ADC Channel Analog-Input Mode Sequencer Registers.

detaileddescription.para: The sequencer must be in the Safe Mode before writing to these registers.

parameterdescription.para: Bit mask of all the channels for which the input mode is differential mode. Use XSM_SEQ_CH__* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to specify the channel numbers. Differential input mode is set for bit masks of 1 and unipolar input mode for bit masks of 0. The InputModeChMask is a 32 bit mask that is written to the two 16 bit ADC Channel Analog-Input Mode Sequencer Registers.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the given values were written successfully to the ADC Channel Analog-Input Mode Sequencer Registers.
XST_FAILURE if the channel sequencer is enabled.

briefdescription.para: Gets the analog input mode for all channels from the ADC Channel Analog-Input Mode Sequencer Registers.

simplesect.para: The input mode for all the channels. Use XSM_SEQ_CH_* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the Channel numbers. Bit masks of 1 are the channels for which input mode is differential and bit mask of 0 are the channels for which input mode is unipolar.

briefdescription.para: Sets the number of acquisition cycles in the ADC Channel Acquisition Time Sequencer Registers.

detaileddescription.para: The sequencer must be in the Safe Mode before writing to these registers.

parameterdescription.para: Bit mask of all the channels for which the number of acquisition cycles is to be extended. Use XSM_SEQ_CH__* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to specify the Channel numbers. Acquisition cycles are extended to 10 ADCCLK cycles for bit masks of 1 and are the default 4 ADCCLK cycles for bit masks of 0. The AcqCyclesChMask is a 32 bit mask that is written to the two 16 bit ADC Channel Acquisition Time Sequencer Registers.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the given values were written successfully to the Channel Sequencer Registers.
XST_FAILURE if the channel sequencer is enabled.

briefdescription.para: Gets the acquisition status from the ADC Channel Acquisition Time Sequencer Registers.

simplesect.para: The acquisition time for all the channels. Use XSM_SEQ_CH__* defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the Channel numbers. Bit masks of 1 are the channels for which acquisition cycles are extended and bit mask of 0 are the channels for which acquisition cycles are not extended.

briefdescription.para: Sets the contents of the given Alarm Threshold Register.

parameterdescription.para: Index of an Alarm Threshold Register to be set. Use XSM_ATR_* constants defined in xsysmon.h to specify the index.
16-bit threshold value to write into the register.

simplesect.para: Over Temperature upper threshold is programmable only in V6, 7 Series/Zynq XADC and UltraScale. BRAM high and low voltage threshold registers are available only in 7 Series XADC and UltraScale. VUSER0 to VUSER3 threshold registers are available only in UltraScale. All the remaining Alarm Threshold registers specified by the constants XSM_ATR_*, are available in all the families of the Sysmon.

briefdescription.para: Returns the contents of the specified Alarm Threshold Register.

parameterdescription.para: Index of an Alarm Threshold Register to be read. Use XSM_ATR_* constants defined in xsysmon.h to specify the index.

simplesect.para: A 16-bit value representing the contents of the selected Alarm Threshold Register.

Over Temperature upper threshold is programmable only in V6 and 7 Series XADC BRAM high and low voltage threshold registers are available only in 7 Series and Zynq XADC. All the remaining Alarm Threshold registers specified by the constants XSM_ATR_*, are available in all the families of the Sysmon.

briefdescription.para: Sets the powerdown temperature for the OverTemp signal in the OT Powerdown register.

parameterdescription.para: 16-bit OT Upper Alarm Register powerdown value. Valid values are 0 to 0x0FFF.

simplesect.para: This API has been deprecated. Use XSysMon_SetAlarmThreshold(), instead. This API should be used only with V6/7 Series since the upper threshold of OverTemp is programmable in in only V6 SysMon/7 Series and Zynq XADC.

briefdescription.para: Returns the powerdown temperature of the OverTemp signal in the OT Powerdown register.

simplesect.para: A 12-bit OT Upper Alarm Register powerdown value.

This API has been deprecated. Use XSysMon_GetAlarmThreshold(), instead. This API should be used only with V6/7 Series since the upper threshold of OverTemp is programmable in only V6 SysMon/7 Series and Zynq XADC.

briefdescription.para: Enables programming of the powerdown temperature for the OverTemp signal in the OT Powerdown register.

simplesect.para: This API should be used only with V6/7 Series since the upper threshold of OverTemp is programmable in only V6 SysMon/7 Series and Zynq XADC.

briefdescription.para: Disables programming of the powerdown temperature for the OverTemp signal in the OT Powerdown register.

simplesect.para: This API should be used only with V6 SysMon/7 Series and Zynq XADC since the upper threshold of OverTemp is programmable in only V6 SysMon/7 Series and Zynq XADC.

briefdescription.para: Enables the temperature update logic so that the temperature can be sent over the TEMP_OUT port.
Disables the temperature update logic for the TEMP_OUT port.
Sets the number of wait cycles for the temperature update logic.

simplesect.para: The default number of wait cycles are 1000(0x3E8).

briefdescription.para: Looks up the device configuration based on the unique device ID.

detaileddescription.para: The table XSysMon_ConfigTable contains the configuration info for each device in the system.

listitem.para: A pointer to the configuration found.
NULL if the specified device ID was not found.

briefdescription.para: Runs a self-test on the driver/device.

detaileddescription.para:
The test:
Resets the device,
Writes a value into the Alarm Threshold register and reads it back for comparison.
Resets the device again.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the value read from the Alarm Threshold register is the same as the value written.
XST_FAILURE Otherwise.

simplesect.para: This is a destructive test in that resets of the device are performed. Refer to the device specification for the device status after the reset operation.

briefdescription.para: Enables the global interrupt in the Global Interrupt Enable Register.

detaileddescription.para: Enabling the global interrupt in the Global Interrupt Enable Register (GIER) enables the interrupt output from the System Monitor/ADC device. Interrupts enabled using XSysMon_IntrEnable() do not occur until the global interrupt enable bit is set by using this function.

simplesect.para: The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Disables the global interrupt in the Global Interrupt Enable Register.

detaileddescription.para: Disabling the global interrupt in the Global Interrupt Enable Register (GIER) disables the interrupt output from the System Monitor/ADC device.

simplesect.para: The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Enables the specified interrupts in the device.

detaileddescription.para: Interrupts enabled using this function do not occur until the global interrupt enable bit is set by using the XSysMon_IntrGlobalEnable()function.

parameterdescription.para: Bit-mask of the interrupts to be enabled. Bit positions set to 1 enable the interrupt. Bit positions set to 0 keep the previous setting. This mask is formed by OR'ing XSM_IPIXR_* bits defined in xsysmon_hw.h.

simplesect.para: The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Disables the specified interrupts in the device.

parameterdescription.para: Bit-mask of the interrupts to be disabled. Bit positions set to 1 disable the interrupt. Bit positions set to 0 keep the previous setting. This mask is formed by OR'ing XSM_IPIXR_* bits defined in xsysmon_hw.h.

simplesect.para: The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Returns the enabled interrupts read from the Interrupt Enable Register (IPIER).

detaileddescription.para: Use the XSM_IPIXR_* constants defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the returned value.

simplesect.para: A 32-bit value representing the contents of the IPIER.
The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Returns the interrupt status read from the Interrupt Status Register (IPISR).

detaileddescription.para: Use the XSM_IPIXR_* constants defined in xsysmon_hw.h to interpret the returned value.

simplesect.para: A 32-bit value representing the contents of the IPISR.
The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Clears the specified interrupts in the Interrupt Status Register (IPISR).

parameterdescription.para: Bit-mask of the interrupts to be cleared. Bit positions set to 1 clear the interrupts. Bit positions of 0 do not change the previous interrupt status. This mask is formed by OR'ing XSM_IPIXR_* bits defined in xsysmon_hw.h.

simplesect.para: The device must be configured at hardware build time to include interrupt component for this function to work.

briefdescription.para: Checks if the SysMonitor/ADC device is in Event Sampling mode.

listitem.para: TRUE if the device is in Event Sampling Mode.
FALSE if the device is in Continuous Sampling Mode.

simplesect.para: C-Style signature: int XSysMon_IsEventSamplingModeSet(XSysMon *InstancePtr);

briefdescription.para: Checks if a Dynamic Reconfiguration Port (DRP) transaction from the JTAG is in progress.

listitem.para: TRUE if the DRP transaction from JTAG is in Progress.
FALSE if there is no DRP transaction from the JTAG.

simplesect.para: C-Style signature: int XSysMon_IsDrpBusy(XSysMon *InstancePtr);

briefdescription.para: Checks if the Dynamic Reconfiguration Port (DRP) is locked by the JTAG.

listitem.para: TRUE if the DRP is locked by the JTAG.
FALSE if the DRP is not locked by the JTAG.

simplesect.para: C-Style signature: int XSysMon_IsDrpLocked(XSysMon *InstancePtr);

briefdescription.para: Converts System Monitor/ADC raw data to temperature in centigrades.

simplesect.para: The Temperature in centigrades.
C-Style signature: float XSysMon_RawToTemperature(u32 AdcData);

briefdescription.para: Converts System Monitor/ADC raw data to voltage in volts.

simplesect.para: The Voltage in volts.
C-Style signature: float XSysMon_RawToVoltage(u32 AdcData);

briefdescription.para: Converts temperature in centigrades to System Monitor/ADC raw data.

parameterdescription.para: Temperature in centigrades to be converted to System Monitor/ADC Raw Data.

simplesect.para: The System Monitor/ADC Raw Data.
C-Style signature: int XSysMon_TemperatureToRaw(float Temperature);

briefdescription.para: Converts voltage in volts to System Monitor/ADC raw data.

parameterdescription.para: Voltage in volts to be converted to System Monitor/ADC Raw Data.

simplesect.para: The System Monitor/ADC Raw Data.
C-Style signature: int XSysMon_VoltageToRaw(float Voltage);

Declares the driver API for the System Monitor/ADC device.

detaileddescription.para: The XSysMon driver supports the Xilinx System Monitor/ADC device.

The System Monitor/ADC device has the following features:
10-bit, 200-KSPS (kilo samples per second) Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC)
Monitoring of on-chip supply voltages and temperature
1 dedicated differential analog-input pair and 16 auxiliary differential analog-input pairs
Automatic alarms based on user defined limits for the on-chip supply voltages and temperature
Automatic Channel Sequencer, programmable averaging, programmable acquisition time for the external inputs, unipolar or differential input selection for the external inputs
Inbuilt Calibration
Optional interrupt request generation
External Mux (7 Series and Zynq XADC)
The user should refer to the hardware device specification for detailed information about the device.
This header file contains the prototypes of driver functions that can be used to access the System Monitor/ADC device.
The System Monitor Channel Sequencer supports the following operating modes:

listitem.para: Default : This is the default mode after power up. In this mode of operation the System Monitor operates in a sequence mode, monitoring the on chip sensors: Temperature, VCCINT, and VCCAUX.
One pass through sequence : In this mode the System Monitor converts the channels enabled in the Sequencer Channel Enable registers for a single pass and then stops.
Continuous cycling of sequence : In this mode the System Monitor converts the channels enabled in the Sequencer Channel Enable registers continuously.

Single channel mode: In this mode the System Monitor Channel Sequencer is disabled and the System Monitor operates in a Single Channel Mode. The System Monitor can operate either in a Continuous or Event driven sampling mode in the single channel mode.
Simultaneous sampling mode: This mode is available only in 7 Series and Zynq XADC devices. In this mode both ADCs sample and digitize two different analog input signals at the same time.

Independent ADC mode: This mode is available only in 7 Series and Zynq XADC devices. In this mode ADC A is used to implement a fixed monitoring mode which is similar to default mode, but the fixed alarm functions are enabled. ADC B is available to be used with the external analog input channels only.

detaileddescription.para: The device driver enables higher layer software (for example, an application) to communicate to the System Monitor/ADC device.

XSysMon_CfgInitialize() API is used to initialize the System Monitor/ADC device. The user needs to first call the XSysMon_LookupConfig() API which returns the Configuration structure pointer which is passed as a parameter to the XSysMon_CfgInitialize() API.
The System Monitor/ADC device supports interrupt driven mode and the default operation mode is polling mode.
The interrupt mode is available only if hardware is configured to support interrupts.

This driver does not provide a Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) for the device. It is the responsibility of the application to provide one if needed. Refer to the interrupt example provided with this driver for details on using the device in interrupt mode.
This driver supports Virtual Memory. The RTOS is responsible for calculating the correct device base address in Virtual Memory space.
This driver is not thread safe. Any needs for threads or thread mutual exclusion must be satisfied by the layer above this driver.

Asserts are used within all Xilinx drivers to enforce constraints on argument values. Asserts can be turned off on a system-wide basis by defining, at compile time, the NDEBUG identifier. By default, asserts are turned on and it is recommended that users leave asserts on during development.
The XSysMon driver is composed of several source files. This allows the user to build and link only those parts of the driver that are necessary.

System Monitor/ADC device can be accessed through the JTAG port and the AXI interface. The driver implementation does not support the simultaneous access of the device by both these interfaces. The user has to care of this situation in the user application code.
